content: The fourth edition of the World Health Organization's Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality, which incorporates the first and second addenda, builds upon over 60 years of WHO guidance on drinking-water quality. This guidance has served as an authoritative foundation for the development of national regulations and standards aimed at ensuring water safety to protect public health. This edition represents the outcome of significant revisions designed to clarify and expand upon the methods for implementing its recommendations. These include contextual hazard identification and risk management through the establishment of health-based targets, water safety plans spanning from catchment to consumer, and independent surveillance mechanisms. The updated guidelines reflect a renewed emphasis on primary prevention strategies. The document provides substantial additional guidance on best practices, incorporating changes introduced in the third edition. It includes new risk assessments for a range of emerging chemical and microbial hazards, as well as their application to various pesticides used for public health purposes. Existing reviews of chemicals and waterborne pathogens have been updated to reflect the latest scientific information. The chapter addressing radiological aspects of drinking-water quality has undergone a comprehensive update. Compared to the previous edition, this new version, which includes the first and second addenda, places greater emphasis on practical, achievable measures and the development of sound regulations. These regulations are designed to be applicable across low-income, middle-income, and industrialized countries alike. The guidelines aim to prevent potential health crises arising from the consumption of unsafe drinking water, particularly in the context of rapid urbanization, water scarcity, and climate change.
